holidays.name: Fudge Day
holidays.description: A day for indulging in rich, creamy squares of chocolatey (or peanut buttery, or maple-y) fudge. Bakers and candy makers whip up batches, and everyone else politely volunteers as taste testers.
holidays.origin: National Fudge Day is an unofficial food observance listed in many holiday calendars. Fudge itself is traditionally credited to a 'fudged' batch of caramels in the 1880s, and Vassar College students helped popularize it.
holidays.funFact: Fudge reportedly got its name from the old slang word 'fudge,' meaning to botch something, because the first batch was an accident. In 1888, Vassar student Emelyn Hartridge made a batch and sold 30 pounds of it at a campus event.

holidays.name: Bloomsday
holidays.description: Fans of James Joyce's novel Ulysses dress in Edwardian clothing, read aloud from the book, and eat the kinds of foods the characters eat, like gorgonzola sandwiches and burgundy wine, with some Dubliners going for a full breakfast of kidneys.
holidays.origin: The day is set on June 16, 1904, the single day on which the entire novel takes place. It was first celebrated in 1954, on the 50th anniversary, when a group of Irish writers did a pilgrimage around Dublin.
holidays.funFact: Joyce picked June 16, 1904 because it was the date of his first outing with Nora Barnacle, the woman who would become his wife.

holidays.name: International Day of Family Remittances
holidays.description: A day honoring the hundreds of millions of migrant workers who send money home to support their families, and the huge global impact of these small but vital transfers.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly established the observance in 2015, with the first one held on June 16, 2015, to recognize how remittances help families and communities worldwide.
holidays.funFact: Remittances to low- and middle-income countries have totaled hundreds of billions of dollars a year, often surpassing foreign direct investment and official development aid.

holidays.name: Juneteenth Eve Cookout Prep Day / Father's Day Season Fly Fishing Day
holidays.description: Anglers celebrate the hobby of fly fishing, tying flies, and standing in cold rivers wearing waders and contemplating life, usually while catching nothing.
holidays.origin: Fishing and outdoor groups have long promoted mid-June as prime time for fly fishing, and sporting communities treat the pre-Father's Day period as an unofficial celebration.
holidays.funFact: Fly fishing is thought to date back to at least the 2nd century, when the Roman writer Claudius Aelianus described Macedonian anglers using lures made of red wool and feathers.

holidays.name: Day of the African Child
holidays.description: An annual observance that spotlights the education and rights of children across Africa, with events, speeches, and school activities to promote learning and well-being.
holidays.origin: It honors the students killed in the 1976 Soweto Uprising in South Africa, who were protesting inferior education under apartheid. The Organisation of African Unity first established it in 1991.
holidays.funFact: The Soweto Uprising began on June 16, 1976, when thousands of schoolchildren marched against being forced to learn in Afrikaans, and it became a turning point in the struggle against apartheid.
